messages:
jane: heads-up — MatchaPay (customer) opened an escalation: p95 latency jumped after last night's runtime rollout. dashboard shows p95 from ~220ms -> ~680ms for /v1/generate across eu-west.

mike: on it. which rollout? full runtime v2.8 yesterday 23:10 UTC. any request ids from the customer?

support-bot: forwarded incident INC-2456. customer provided sample req id rq_84b2f1c. Payload size ~1.2k tokens.

sara: grabbing traces for rq_84b2f1c now. Seeing long queue_wait_ms ~420ms on node runtime-eu-3 before kernel dispatch.

alex: interesting — canary toggled new kernel_selector logic that prefers fused-attn-v2 for long sequences. that landed in runtime v2.8.

mike: can we reproduce quickly? running a few synthetic requests with same token distribution and model variant.

chris: repro script:
```bash
for i in {1..20}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","prompt":"<matchapay-sim>","max_tokens":1024}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' &
done
```

sara: ran 50 samples against canary pool. median ok, but p95/p99 show big tail~600-900ms. logs show batch_window_ms=20 and batch sizes spike to 32 for these requests.

alex: fused-attn-v2 has slightly slower single-request latency but better throughput; combined with batch_window_ms=20 it looks like it creates high queueing for some short bursts.

mike: propose two quick mitigations: 1) rollback kernel_selector on a small subset of nodes to prefer fused-attn-v1; 2) reduce batch_window_ms to 8ms for customer-facing pools. which is lower risk?

jane: we need fast customer relief. prefer minimal surface: change batch_window_ms for matchapay route first, then partial rollback if needed.

sara: applied runtime config patch to route "customer:matchapay" -> batch_window_ms: 8, kvcache_ttl: 600 on eu-west pool. pushing to 2 nodes as canary at 23:27 UTC.

ops-bot: deploy event: config update applied to runtime-eu-3 nodes (2/2) by sara at 23:27:12 UTC.

mike: monitoring... p95 for matchapay route dropped to ~250ms on those nodes within 2 minutes. p99 improving but still elevated.

chris: started incremental rollback of kernel_selector on runtime-eu-3 -> prefer fused-attn-v1 for matchapay traffic. rolling to 4 nodes.

support-bot: MatchaPay confirms degradation gone on new requests routed to canary. "Thanks, latency looks normal now."

jane: great. can we capture root cause summary for postmortem? also need follow-ups for SLA credit/comms.

alex: root cause (short): new kernel_selector + high batch_window_ms caused larger-than-expected batching for their request distribution, increasing queue wait time and p95. fused-attn-v2 is fine for throughput but not for their bursty pattern.

sara: action items:
- roll the kernel_selector rollback to all eu-west customer pools for the next 30m while we validate.
- add synthetic daily smoke that hits MatchaPay-like token distributions (1k tokens) and asserts p95 < 350ms.
- add automated alert: route-level p95 > 400ms for 5m.
- update rollout checklist: perf profile check for kernel selector + batch config combos.

mike: I'll start rollback to remaining nodes and coordinate with release; tagging this as P1 until done.

jane: assign ownership for postmortem: sara (lead), alex (root cause), chris (mitigation docs), mike (monitoring/alerts).

sara: noted. I'll draft RCA and postmortem, include perf traces and the specific req ids (rq_84b2f1c, rq_92cd3a7).

ops-bot: note — billing/SLA team notified for potential credit discussion.

jane: closing loop with MatchaPay and will schedule postmortem review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. thanks team :thumbsup:
